questions.question: What flaw in the original real primitive recursive framework motivates the paper's careful treatment of partial functions?

options.A: Ambiguity about domains and differential recursion on partial functions undermines some claims
options.B: Its functions were all discontinuous and therefore lacked derivatives
options.C: Its base class omitted integer constants
options.D: It used only discrete time and could not discuss real-valued inputs

questions.rationale: The paper argues that domain behavior was underspecified, creating ambiguous or erroneous statements.
questions.evidence_quote: the definition of the classes suffers from ambiguity

questions.question: How does the paper formulate 'unique' solutions for differential recursion when functions may be partial?

options.A: A solution is unique if every other solution restricts to it on its domain
options.B: It is the solution with the largest derivative at zero
options.C: It is any solution defined on a bounded interval containing zero
options.D: It is the solution with the smallest possible domain

questions.rationale: This restriction-based definition selects the maximal-domain solution up to restriction.
questions.evidence_quote: we say that a function h ∈ H is unique in H if the restriction of any function in H to dom h is a restriction of h

questions.question: Under what regularity assumptions does the paper show that all solutions of the differential-recursion equation are restrictions of the selected solution?

options.A: If g is analytic with open domain
options.C: If g is measurable and integrable
options.D: Only if both f and g are polynomials

questions.rationale: Theorem 12(a) uses analyticity of g on an open domain, invoking uniqueness for initial-value problems.
questions.evidence_quote: If g is an analytic4 function with open domain

questions.question: What counterexample shows that Campagnolo's relaxed operator drC can break analyticity?

options.A: Integrating 1/√|t−1| yields a total function with a kink at t=1
options.B: Integrating exp(t) yields a nowhere-continuous function
options.C: Taking a square root on positive inputs creates an oscillatory function
options.D: A constant integrand yields two solutions with distinct initial values

questions.rationale: The isolated singularity allowed by drC produces a continuous but nondifferentiable result at the singular point.

questions.question: What domain distinction does the author highlight when comparing the two recursion operators for square root?

options.A: With dr the constructed sqrt+ has domain (0,∞), while drC can extend it to [0,∞)
options.B: dr gives [0,∞), while drC restricts sqrt+ to (0,∞)
options.C: Both operators require sqrt+ to be defined on all real numbers
options.D: Neither operator can construct square root without minimization

questions.rationale: The singular integrand at the endpoint is admitted only under the relaxed clause, changing the domain.
questions.evidence_quote: with drC, the same equation produces the square root function defined on [0, ∞), rather than on (0, ∞)

questions.question: What closure result does the paper prove for differential algebraicity under its two basic operators?

options.A: Juxtaposition and composition preserve the property
options.B: Only juxtaposition preserves it; composition can never do so
options.C: Composition preserves it only for total polynomial functions
options.D: Neither operator preserves it when domains are open

questions.rationale: Theorem 8 establishes preservation under both operations, assuming the relevant functions are differentially algebraic.
questions.evidence_quote: The property of being differentially algebraic is preserved by jx and cm.

questions.question: Which characterization helps establish differential algebraicity for multivariate analytic functions in the paper?

options.A: All derivatives lie in a field generated by a finite subset of derivatives
options.B: Every partial derivative must be identically zero
options.C: The function must have a globally convergent Taylor series on all ℝᵐ
options.D: A single polynomial must relate all mixed partial derivatives of every order simultaneously

questions.rationale: Lemma 5 characterizes differential algebraicity via finite generation of the derivative field.
questions.evidence_quote: D f ⊆R(B) for some finite set B ⊆D f

questions.question: How does the paper refute Moore's claim that all real primitive recursive functions are differentially algebraic?

options.A: A finite-cutoff integral approximation to Γ is primitive recursive, but differential algebraicity would pass to the Γ limit and contradict Hölder's theorem
options.B: It proves sin is primitive recursive but not analytic
options.C: It finds that reciprocal is discontinuous on its domain
options.D: It shows every primitive-recursive function has compact domain

questions.rationale: The truncated gamma integral is primitive recursive and differential algebraicity would imply a differential equation for Γ in the limit.
questions.evidence_quote: contrary to Claim 1, it is not differentially algebraic

questions.question: Why does the paper avoid treating differential recursion as equivalent to the pointwise differential equation alone?

options.A: On partial domains, solution intervals and integrand-definedness matter; unrestricted treatment can admit non-analytic or nonunique outcomes
options.B: The integral equation cannot be differentiated even for analytic functions
options.C: The differential equation requires integer-valued time
options.D: Pointwise equations cannot represent total functions

questions.rationale: The definitions explicitly specify domain and uniqueness behavior to prevent ambiguities, especially with singularities.
questions.evidence_quote: The clauses (a)–(c) of Definition 9 guarantee that the integral equation (9) makes sense for all t ∈dom h.

questions.question: What research direction does the author identify after the failure of Claim 1?

options.A: Find a simply defined subclass of real primitive recursive functions closely related to differentially algebraic functions
options.B: Prove that the gamma function is differentially algebraic
options.C: Replace all real functions with Turing-machine configurations
options.D: Show that differential recursion is identical to minimization

questions.rationale: The stated open problem seeks a useful subclass restoring a close analog-computation connection.
questions.evidence_quote: Find a subclass of our real primitive recursive functions, preferably with an equally simple definition, that has a close relationship to the differentially algebraic functions.
